maths-2025-hl-p1-q10-e-i.description: Question 10 defines a sequence of dot patterns on the coordinate plane. H(n) is the total number of dots in Pattern n. Part (i) asks for H(1). For natural n, H(n + 1) = H(n) + 2n + 3. Part (ii) asks for an induction proof that H(n) = (n + 1)² for every natural n.

maths-2025-hl-p2-q8-a-i.description: A square-based pyramid has a 6 m square base ABCD. The diagonals meet at O, P is directly above O, and the four congruent triangular faces have PA = PB = 11 m. Part (i) asks the student to use Pythagoras to show that OB = 3√2 m and then find the vertical height OP in surd form.

maths-2025-hl-p2-q8-a-ii.description: A square-based pyramid has a 6 m square base ABCD, with P directly above the centre O, and PA = PB = 11 m. On triangular face PAB, angle PAB is 74.2 degrees to one decimal place. Part (ii) asks for the total area of the four triangular roof faces, to the nearest square metre.

maths-2025-hl-p2-q8-a-iii.description: A square-based pyramid has a 6 m square base ABCD and four congruent triangular faces with PA = PB = 11 m. A scaled partial net shows the square base and two triangular sides. Part (iii) asks the student to construct the rest of the net and show all construction lines.

maths-2025-hl-p2-q10-e.description: A maths test gives a student 0, 1, 2, or 3 marks on one question with respective proportions 0.19, p, 2r, and r, where p and r are non-negative real numbers. Part (e) asks for the largest possible expected mark.
